o.text: By surface analysis, izafet I compound of el (“people”) + xan (“khan”).
Borrowed from Persian هموطن (hamvatan). By surface analysis, həm- + vətən.
From Arabic نَغْمَة (naḡma), from Ancient Greek νεῦμα (neûma).

From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (qonuq). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kon- (“spend the night”), whence also Azerbaijani qonşu (“neighbour”) and Azerbaijani qonaq (“guest”). Compare Turkish konuk (“guest”), Crimean Tatar qonaq (“meeting room”), Chuvash хӑна (hăna, “guest”).
